identity.title: Central line exit-site erythema, tenderness, or purulence (with line-day count)

technique.how: Remove the dressing and inspect the insertion/exit site and tunnel in good light: erythema (note extent in cm), induration or swelling, tenderness on palpation, and purulent exudate (express gently along the tunnel). Record catheter type (non-tunneled vs tunneled/cuffed), site, and line-day count.
technique.prerequisites: Dressing change with clean technique; knowledge of insertion date and catheter type.
technique.contraindications: None; do not delay blood cultures or catheter management while inspecting.

interpretation.positive_finding: Purulence, tenderness, or erythema >=2 cm at the exit site indicates local catheter infection and, in a febrile or hypotensive patient, should raise concern for catheter-related bloodstream infection with S. aureus or Gram-negative organisms.
interpretation.negative_finding: A clean, non-inflamed site does not exclude catheter-related bloodstream infection; most short-term CVC infections (largely coagulase-negative staphylococci) show little or no local inflammation.
interpretation.pitfalls: Local inflammation is insensitive (near zero) for CRBSI with short-term non-cuffed CVCs; dressing adhesive irritation and tunnel-line manipulation can mimic erythema. Hemodialysis exit-site scale evidence uses a skin-swab culture reference, not bacteremia.
interpretation.changes_what: Positive site: culture exudate, draw paired blood cultures, consider line removal; negative site does not lower suspicion of CRBSI in an unexplained fever or shock.

estimates.target_condition: COMPOSITE: exit-site infection of tunneled hemodialysis CVC (3-item scale: interdialytic exit-site pain OR erythema >=2 cm OR abscess/purulent exudate)
estimates.population: Adults with tunneled hemodialysis CVC in place >=1 month; 337 catheters, 310 patients, 515 pericatheter cultures; multicenter prospective cohort
estimates.reference_standard: Positive pericatheter skin swab culture (taken only when any scale item present)

sources.citation: Safdar N, Maki DG. Inflammation at the insertion site is not predictive of catheter-related bloodstream infection with short-term, noncuffed central venous catheters. Crit Care Med. 2002.

Cobo-Sanchez JL, Blanco-Mavillard I, Pelayo-Alonso R, Mancebo-Salas N, Fernandez-Fernandez I, Larraneta-Inda I, et al. Validation of a Clinical Scale for Early Detection of Infections at the Exit Site of Central Venous Catheters for Hemodialysis. Kidney Int Rep. 2024.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use a clean site to rule out CRBSI in short-term non-cuffed CVCs; do not rely on site appearance in neutropenic patients who may not mount local inflammation.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Fever with hypotension plus any line in situ: cultures and sepsis pathway regardless of site appearance; purulent exit site with sepsis mandates line removal.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: No kappa for bedside site inspection found in the sources reviewed; Safdar used trained research nurses with a 0-5 inflammation score.

extraction_notes: Anchor study Safdar & Maki (PMID 12483050; ICU, 1263 short-term non-cuffed CVCs, 35 CRBSI by DNA subtyping) reports only a range for local inflammation: 'The sensitivity of local inflammation for diagnosis of CVC-related BSI was dismal (0-3%)' (Abstract, Results); per RANGES rule no point value entered, and the specificity is not given in the abstract (full text not open access). The only sens/spec pair found is the Cobo-Sanchez 2024 3-item exit-site scale for tunneled HD catheters, entered as COMPOSITE; its reference standard is a skin-swab culture (exit-site infection), not bacteremia, and cultures were taken only when an item was present, so specificity is estimated in a selected sample and prevalence is not entered. Line-day count as a quantitative predictor was not found in a diagnostic-accuracy format. Guembe 2014 (PMID 23850957) concerns superficial cultures, not exam, and was not used.
